name: send_message
description: Send {{OWNER}} a WhatsApp message. The only way to reach them. Returned text is just a fallback in the chat and goes nowhere from a scheduled task. Plain text, no markdown. Text like a friend, short, separate thoughts in separate messages, and don't repeat what you already sent. Transcript lines carry message ids, so pass one as reply_to only when a bare message would be ambiguous. To include a credential you can't see, write ${NAME} where it belongs, e.g. client_id=${SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID}, and Tera fills it in on the way out while history keeps the placeholder.

text.description: Message text. Plain, short, no markdown.

image_path.description: Path to an image file: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

video_path.description: Path to a video file: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

audio_path.description: Path to an ordinary audio attachment: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

voice_note_path.description: Path to an Ogg Opus voice note: absolute, or relative to the workspace root. Sends it with WhatsApp's push-to-talk flag.

file_path.description: Path to any other file to send as a WhatsApp document: absolute, or relative to the workspace root

reply_to.description: Message id to quote, as shown in the transcript, e.g. msg_a1b2. Use it when answering one specific message out of several.

name: react
description: React to a message with an emoji. Often the whole reply, for acknowledging or agreeing. Use a reaction or a message to acknowledge, not both.

message_id.description: Internal event id of the message to react to, e.g. msg_a1b2. Not a WhatsApp id.

name: schedule
description: Schedule a one-off or recurring background task. Use this for anything time-based, never cron or launchd. Times are this machine's local time. The run starts on a fresh thread that sees only your prompt and the recent chat, so write `prompt` as standalone instructions: what to do, where to look, and when it's worth messaging {{OWNER}}. If the timing depends on when something actually happens, schedule a single run from that event and reschedule when it happens again, instead of a fixed recurring clock. The response echoes the first run, check it's what you meant.

prompt.description: Standalone instructions for the worker. It sees only this and the last few chat messages. Say what to do, where the inputs are, and when to message {{OWNER}} versus finish silently.

timing.description: When to run. One-off: {"type":"once","at":"2026-08-18T07:30:00+05:30"}, RFC3339 with an offset, in the future. Recurring: {"type":"recurring","rrule":"..."} where rrule is a 5-field cron expression in local time or a fixed interval EVERY_15M / EVERY_2H / EVERY_3D. "30 7 * * *" is 07:30 daily, "0 18 * * MON-FRI" is weekday evenings. Prefer three-letter day names. A cron that restricts both day-of-month and day-of-week is refused, make two schedules. Anything unparseable is rejected.

at.description: One-shot only. RFC3339 with a UTC offset. Must be in the future.

rrule.description: Recurring only. Cron expression in local time, or EVERY_<n>M / EVERY_<n>H / EVERY_<n>D.

name: list_schedules
description: List active schedules with their next run in local time. Check it before creating something that may already exist, and when something {{OWNER}} says affects a schedule.

name: cancel_schedule
description: Cancel an active schedule. Cancel ones that stopped being useful, and cancel and recreate one whose timing changed.

schedule_id.description: Schedule ID to cancel, e.g. sched_a1b2

name: request_secret
description: Ask {{OWNER}} for a credential a skill needs: an API key, client ID or token. Sends them a short message and claims their next message as the value, which Tera stores where skills read it. You never see the value, not now and not later. It is taken out of the message before it reaches you, so there is no point asking for it in plain conversation and no point reading it back to check. Always use this rather than asking in your own words: a credential typed into an ordinary message ends up in history, in the JSONL projection, and in every memory generation built from it. Check `.runtime/secrets.json` first, it may already be stored. The request expires in 15 minutes.

name.description: Env-var shaped name: A-Z, digits and underscore, starting with an uppercase letter, e.g. SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID

reason.description: What it is for, as a short phrase completing 'I need NAME to ...'. Shown to {{OWNER}} verbatim, e.g. 'control your Spotify'.
